veranderings.blok: Lyn, vorm en kleur in letters en patrone
veranderings.rede: For two colours contrasting with each other, 'teen mekaar afsteek' is the idiomatic Afrikaans; 'teen mekaar uitstaan' is less natural.
A bare 'so' at the end of the sentence is vague for Grade 5; 'op dié manier' makes the link back to the previous sentences clear.

veranderings.voor: Dieselfde woorde geld ook vir die liggaam.
veranderings.na: Dieselfde woorde geld ook vir liggaamsversiering.
veranderings.rede: The art-element words apply to the decoration, not to the body itself; naming the lesson's own term makes the sentence say what it means.

veranderings.voor: na letters en patrone en na 'n kraalkraag
veranderings.rede: The double 'en ... en na' is clumsy; a plain list of three reads more smoothly with the same meaning.

veranderings.blok: Jou eie werk en jou omgewing
veranderings.voor: Sê dan met hierdie les se woorde wat jy sien.
veranderings.na: Gebruik dan hierdie les se woorde om te sê wat jy sien.
veranderings.rede: The inserted phrase between 'Sê' and its object makes the sentence hard to follow; this order is clearer for Grade 5.
'Mee' needs something to refer to; 'om dinge mee te kleur' is the complete, standard construction.

vlae.teks: Baie klein krale styf langs mekaar gee 'n knopperige tekstuur.
vlae.rede: 'Baie klein krale' can be read as 'very small beads' or 'many small beads'; 'baie' is protected and the intended meaning cannot be chosen without guessing, so the writer should decide.

vlae.teks: 'n Gekleurde grond, soos rooi of geel, wat mense fynmaak om mee te kleur.
vlae.rede: 'soos rooi of geel' attaches to 'grond', so it reads as if a soil is like a colour; a rewording such as naming red or yellow soil would be clearer, but it touches a definition, so it is left to the reviewer or writer.
